originalBehavior: The route should remain a longform Engineering Sandbox article with a shared hero, generated story rail, and local provenance handling.
localStatus: The route still uses the shared Engineering Sandbox shell while keeping all public teaching content local to the Formula 1 route.
notes: The shell provides the longform wrapper and generated chapter navigation.
Public provenance remains neutral because the route is an original local build.
evidence: The route hero, generated chapter rail, and mobile chapter navigation are mounted by the shared shell.
The public route still uses neutral provenance handling rather than an upstream reference page.

originalBehavior: The route should use the Bartosz-family base runtime for shared controls and math utilities, with the file kept unmodified.
localStatus: The route now ships a local copy of base.js and base.css so sliders, segmented controls, touch handlers, ArcBall rotation, and shared math helpers are available inside the Formula 1 route itself.
notes: The local base runtime is intended to stay unmodified unless the route explicitly forks that engine.
The Formula 1 route uses the runtime directly rather than only imitating its control patterns.
evidence: The route head now loads ./js/base.js and ./css/base.css before the route-specific runtime.
The overview scene uses ArcBall rotation and the route controls use Slider and SegmentedControl instances from the base runtime.

originalBehavior: The route should feel closer to the Bartosz family by drawing key scenes procedurally instead of relying on static infographic panels.
localStatus: The route now renders the overview, airflow, front-wing, floor, rear-wing, chassis, power, tyre, braking, track, racecraft, setup, weather, pit, and lap scenes procedurally on canvas, with the overview and aero chapters pushed toward fuller pseudo-3D geometry.
notes: The drawings are explanatory and stylized rather than scan-based or model-import-based.
The route uses procedural silhouettes, animated flow lines, shaded bands, and dynamic traces to make the scenes feel more alive.
Recent updates increased the depth and lighting of the overview and aero chapters so they read less like flat dashboards and more like procedural pseudo-3D scenes.
evidence: Each chapter scene mounts through a drawer_container instead of static metric-card dashboards.
The route runtime draws and repaints scene state directly on canvas in response to base-runtime controls.

originalBehavior: Track, setup, floor posture, power, tyre, braking, and weather decisions should connect back into a shared lap-time story rather than living as isolated widgets.
localStatus: The route keeps a shared Formula 1 state model so track presets, setup sliders, live floor posture, live tyre condition, braking balance, power maps, and weather propagate into the lap-builder scene and chapter summaries.
notes: Track presets change setup, tyre, power, and lap-plan defaults together.
The live floor controls model the platform during the lap while setup ride height remains the selected baseline.
Pit timing remains a separate race-strategy calculation because the final scene models one lap rather than a stint or race.
evidence: Selecting a new track preset updates setup sliders, tyre compound, power mode, power bias, and lap plan together.
Changing live floor ride height or pitch updates floor health, track-weighted sector scores, the speed trace, and the final lap caption.
Changing tyre compound, temperature, load, or stint progress updates tyre health, track-weighted sector scores, speed and braking traces, and the final lap caption.
Changing brake bias or energy recovery updates braking stability, brake-demand-weighted sector scores, speed and braking traces, and the final lap caption.
Weather changes the lap model while pit state remains confined to the pit-strategy scene and caption.

originalBehavior: The Floor and Diffuser chapter should show why platform posture matters and carry that consequence into the final lap rather than ending at a local animation.
localStatus: Named ride-height and pitch controls feed one computeFloorState result for suction, stability, risk, sector loss, trace shape, and the final floor contribution.
notes: Track-specific weights make floor posture matter most on high-speed circuits and sectors.
The result is deliberately explanatory rather than telemetry-grade, CFD-derived, or suspension-simulated.
Tyre condition now has a separate attributed loss so floor and tyre explanations do not overwrite each other.
evidence: The floor scene and caption consume the same computed health state as the lap model.
The lap canvas labels all three sector deltas and the lap caption identifies the floor-attributed loss.
Focused smoke drives live ride height to its keyboard maximum and verifies changed floor and lap captions, high platform risk, and nonzero floor loss.

originalBehavior: The Tyres chapter should explain how compound, thermal state, load, and stint wear become lap performance rather than ending at a local tyre animation.
localStatus: One computeTyreState result now drives the tyre scene, condition label, track-weighted sector loss, speed and braking traces, and tyre-attributed lap loss.
notes: The bounded grip penalty activates below the model's usable grip threshold and is weighted by each circuit's sector demands.
The result is a teaching model rather than telemetry, a carcass-temperature solver, or a full tyre-energy simulation.
Pit timing remains outside this single-lap model because it describes race strategy rather than one lap.
evidence: The tyre scene and lap model consume the same compound, temperature, load, stint, wear, grip, and condition state.
The final lap caption reports tyre-attributed loss independently from floor-attributed loss.
Focused smoke drives tyre temperature to its keyboard maximum and verifies overheating plus nonzero tyre-attributed lap loss.

originalBehavior: The Braking chapter should explain how bias and energy recovery alter stability and carry that consequence into the final lap rather than ending at a local load-transfer animation.
localStatus: One computeBrakeState result now drives the braking scene, authority and stability labels, brake-demand-weighted sector loss, speed and braking traces, and brake-attributed lap loss.
notes: Sector weights derive from each circuit's existing brake-demand trace instead of adding another circuit-specific table.
Entry speed remains scene context; brake bias and energy recovery determine the attributed stability penalty.
The result is a teaching model rather than telemetry, a brake-by-wire controller, or a tyre-lock simulation.
evidence: The braking scene, chapter caption, and lap model consume the same authority, rear-rotation, stability, penalty, and condition state.
The final lap caption reports brake-attributed loss independently from floor- and tyre-attributed losses.
Focused smoke drives energy recovery to its keyboard maximum and verifies compromised braking plus nonzero brake-attributed lap loss.

originalBehavior: The final lap canvas should make independently attributed floor, tyre, and braking losses visible without forcing readers to infer them from trace shape or prose alone.
localStatus: The existing lap canvas now renders one compact contribution row for live floor posture, tyre condition, and braking balance while retaining sector deltas, total delta, and the three traces.
notes: The row reuses computeLapState outputs and does not introduce another scene, state model, or attribution calculation.
The mobile canvas uses shorter labels and tighter type while preserving all three values at 320px.
evidence: Floor, tyre, and braking labels repaint with the same values exposed by the final lap caption.
Focused smoke captures canvas text and verifies all three labels against the independently computed caption losses.
A 320px browser check verifies no page overflow and enough canvas width for each compact label.

originalBehavior: Formula 1 controls change procedural scene state and linked captions through pointer and touch interaction.
localStatus: All 42 mounted controls expose visible domain labels and matching accessible names; segmented controls retain Arrow-key selection while sliders retain value semantics plus Arrow, Home, and End behavior.
notes: Every mounted control uses data-control as the shared source for its visible domain label and accessible name.
The two floor controls retain richer directional labels without modifying the shared base runtime.
Reduced-motion preference stops perpetual repainting but repaints scenes after state changes.
evidence: Focused smoke verifies all 42 data-control names against mounted aria labels and rendered visible labels.
Focused smoke uses keyboard input on track, weather, lap-plan, airflow, live floor, tyre-temperature, and energy-recovery controls and verifies linked captions and lap consequences.

originalBehavior: The Route keeps its authored top-level document, runtime roots, and script order.
localStatus: Manifest synchronization owns the body Engineering Sandbox metadata and shared head seams while preserving Route runtime placement.
notes: Ticket 12 synchronizes the manifest-owned Engineering Sandbox body contract and shared head seams without moving existing Route runtimes or scripts.
evidence: Route HTML declares canonical data-story metadata plus one color-scheme meta, synchronous theme init before Route styles, Sandbox CSS after Route styles, and one deferred Sandbox runtime whose existing position is preserved.
